accepted.question_text: For an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), is the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time always at least 1? Equivalently, if T_1^alpha denotes the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version of the process, must c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2 satisfy c^2 >= 1 for every irreducible MMPP?

evidence.quote: Consider the squared coefficient of variation and the limiting index of dispersion of counts given by, c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E^2[T_1^alpha], and d^2 = lim_{t->infty} Var(N(t)) / E[N(t)], where T_1^alpha is the time of the first event, taken from the event stationary version.
Conjecture 4.1. For an irreducible MMPP, c^2 >= 1.

accepted.question_text: For an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), does the first inter-event time in the time-stationary version stochastically dominate the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version? In the paper's notation, if T_1^pi is the first inter-event time under time-stationary initialization and T_1^alpha is the first inter-event time under event-stationary initialization, must T_1^pi >=st T_1^alpha hold for every irreducible MMPP?

evidence.quote: Lemma 2.1. Consider a simple non-transient point process on the line, and let T_1^pi, T_1^alpha represent the first inter-event time in the time-stationary case and event-stationary case respectively.
Conjecture 4.2. For an irreducible MMPP, T_1^pi >=st T_1^alpha.

accepted.question_text: If a Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP) has event-stationary inter-event times with squared coefficient of variation c^2 equal to 1, must the process itself be a Poisson process?

evidence.quote: But, we believe that all MMPPs with c^2 = 1 are Poisson. Yet, we don't have a proof.

accepted.question_text: For a Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), if the squared coefficient of variation c^2 of the event-stationary inter-event times equals 1, does it follow that all modulating Poisson rates lambda_i are equal?

evidence.quote: Further, we believe that for an MMPP, if c^2 = 1 then all lambda_i are equal (the converse is trivially true). We don't have a proof of this either.

accepted.question_text: Do analogues of the two MMPP conjectures extend to general Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions? More specifically, for Cox processes satisfying appropriate regularity assumptions, must the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time be at least 1 and must the time-stationary first inter-event time stochastically dominate the event-stationary first inter-event time?
accepted.context_brief: Cox-process extensions of the MMPP conjectures

evidence.quote: In fact, since any Cox process can be approximated by an MMPP, we believe that versions of conjectures 1 and 2 also hold for Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions.
